text:
Sasha: Quick Q — we're migrating the KMS key used by the vectorizer service (re-encrypt + rotate). Plan is: create new key, add grants for IRSA role, update secret-store to point to new key, then rotate. worried about helm/IRSA race where SA annotation lands after pod starts and CSI secret driver fails to decrypt. Anyone seen this? 

Chris: we've hit that. If helm creates SA + deployment together the mount can race. We used a post-render job to patch the SA annotation and restart the daemonset. 

Amanda: can you paste the Terraform snippets you plan to use for the grant/role? for ordering recs. 

Sasha: here's the minimal snippets — thinking about depends_on: 

```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "vectorizer_key_v2" {
  description = "Vectorizer key v2"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "vectorizer_irsa" {
  name = "vectorizer-irsa-role"
  # assume role with oidc provider
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "irsa_grant" {
  name = "vectorizer-irsa-grant"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.vectorizer_key_v2.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vectorizer_irsa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "ReEncryptFrom", "ReEncryptTo"]
}

# idea: attach a condition limiting use to sts:AssumeRole with session tags
```

Chris: add explicit depends_on between serviceaccount helm chart and the grant apply if you create SA in terraform, but if SA is in helm chart then Terraform can't see it. We solved it by: 
- create IAM role + KMS grant in TF
- add annotation in helm values but use a `post-install` job to patch SA with the role ARN (kubectl patch). That ensures KMS grant already exists. 

Maria: also check the KMS key policy — it must allow the role (or account) to decrypt. Grants are transient and sometimes not sufficient if key policy denies. We grant kms:Decrypt to the role ARN in key policy. 

Ben: For external-secrets/csi case: the CSI driver will attempt decrypt during mount. We added initContainer that waits for SA annotation + a short sleep/retry, then exits; that was enough to avoid flapping. Not ideal but practical. 

Amanda: small terraform ordering tip — if you create an aws_eks_cluster_auth or any data source that reads SA, plan may succeed but apply can reorder. Use `null_resource` with `triggers` referencing resource IDs to enforce ordering where terraform doesn't naturally handle helm -> tf flow. 

infra-bot: CI check: https://ci.example.com/redwood/infra/pipelines/vec-kms-migrate — terraform plan shows `create aws_kms_key` and `create aws_kms_grant` step OK, but helm release shows rollout failing in e2e stage. 

Sasha: cool — i'll do the approach: create key + grant in TF, update key policy, add post-install kubectl patch job in helm chart to annotate SA, and add initContainer wait in deployment. I'll open PR and tag @chris @amanda for review. thanks :pray: 

Chris: ack, ping me when PR is up. I'll sanity check policies + condition edgecases. 

Amanda: +1, i'll look at the terraform ordering and null_resource trick.
